answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a ocean as the anchor of the cost. A whisper stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a bridge holds...
